newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Chirac deems Hungary reliable for paying its debts.
newsitem.headline: Chirac deems Hungary reliable for paying its debts.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, addressing industrialists on the second day of a two-day state visit, praised Hungary on Friday for honouring its debts left by communism.
"Hungary took the decision to honour its debts inherited from the past," Chirac said. "That decision was the right one."
Chirac said as a result Hungarian was seen internationally as a reliable long-term partner which "honoured its word and its signature".

A dozen top French industrialists are accompanying the president, including the chairmen of state electricity and gas companies EDF and GDF, missiles and electronics firm Matra, and construction giant Bouygues.

EDF and GDF have bought stakes worth up to $400 million in Hungary's energy distribution network while Bouygues has a 35 percent stake in the company which built a new stretch of Hungary's southern motorway.
Chirac said such large investments have made France Hungary's third largest investor but she remained only the fifth largest trading partner.
"There seem to be no large deals," he said. "I can understand we are not always the best but I fail to see that we are always the least good."
Aeronautics company are currently vyng with US, Swedish and Russian firms to win an estimated $500 million order to supply Hungary's air force with fighter planes.
On the first day of his visit Chirac set the year 2000 as a target date for Hungary's accession to the European Union, saying it was question of "political will".
To warm applause from his aidience in parliament, Chirac said such a target date was achievable if everyone "made the necessary efforts".
Later he paid tribute to Hungary's failed 1956 revolution when he awarded medals to President Arpad Goncz and 12 other veterans of the uprising.
On Friday Chirac will meet Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn when Hungary's EU and NATO integration are expected to be high on the agenda.
